messages:
priya: hey folks — trying to get local dev environment up (docker-compose -f docker/dev.yml up). Postgres container boots but our init script fails when creating pgvector: ERROR: must be superuser to create extension "vector". Is there a standard dev workaround? I don't want to run everything as root. any advice? :wave:

kevin: welcome @priya! for local dev we usually run Postgres with a superuser so extensions can be created during init. check .env.dev for POSTGRES_PASSWORD and POSTGRES_USER. If missing you can use POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD=trust for dev only. e.g.

kevin: ```
POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD=trust
POSTGRES_USER=postgres
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=
```

maria: if you don't want to change env, another pattern is to build an image that already has the extension installed (we do this for pgvector). See infra/postgres/Dockerfile. Basically `FROM postgres:14` then `RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y postgresql-server-dev-all build-essential && git clone ... && make install` — pain but avoids superuser init step.

jonathan: short workaround: run a one-off psql as the postgres superuser after the container is up, then create the extension. e.g.

jonathan: ```bash
docker-compose -f docker/dev.yml up -d postgres
docker run --rm --network ${PWD##*/}_default --env PGPASSWORD=$(grep POSTGRES_PASSWORD .env.dev | cut -d'=' -f2) postgres:14 \  psql -h postgres -U postgres -c "CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;"
```

priya: thanks! quick question — how do I get the network name `${PWD##*/}_default`? is that the compose project name? :thinking:

kevin: yes it's the compose project name (defaults to your folder). you can also do `docker network ls` and find the one with `dev` in it, or explicitly set COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME in .env.dev.

maria: also double-check our dev Postgres image tag — some of our CI images already have pgvector baked in so `image: redwood/postgres-dev:pgvector-14` might be in docker/dev.yml. if so you don't need any of the above.

priya: ok trying `docker run ... psql` now. will report back. thanks y'all :grin:

devops-bot: reminder: do not commit .env.dev changes that enable trust; that's only for local dev and insecure. Use .env.dev.local for personal overrides.

priya: update — running the one-off psql worked, extension created. migrations run fine now. tagging @kevin and @maria to update README with the `one-off psql` trick? small note: added COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME to my .env.dev.local

kevin: good to add. please put the command under 'Troubleshooting' in README.dev and reference the `pgvector` note. thanks!

maria: thanks for the report, @priya — welcome aboard :tada:
